verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents API keys plus tenant tokens, which are short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. They embed filter rules so a holder sees only permitted data, which gives a least-privilege credential an agent could use for search. The pack does not show action-level or index-level permission scoping for API keys, and nothing ties scoped credentials to agent or MCP use, so it delivers only part of the story. Missing for 10: documented per-action/per-index API key permissions, credential scoping for write/management operations, guidance on scoping keys for agents or the MCP server, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Tenant tokens are short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. They embed search rules (filters) that automatically apply to every search request, ensuring users only see their own data.
Meilisearch uses API keys and tenant tokens to control access to your data.
API keys authenticate requests, while tenant tokens restrict what data each user can see within a shared index.
